ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.claim: The affluent man’s expectation of receiving more is false, and if he opposes the Qur’an he faces a severe penalty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.anchor: This, it is clear, is a totally false claim.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r1.claim: The emphatic denial rebuts the arrogant man's claim: his favors were unearned gifts testing whether he would be grateful or rebellious, and he failed the test.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r1.anchor: they had earned them through their own planning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r2.claim: “Our revelations” means the Qur'an generally, especially its warnings of worldly and next-world punishment and its teaching that God alone governs both realms.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p43/r2.anchor: those who warn them of worldly punishment and the one they will face in the next world

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.claim: God had fully expanded the man's wealth; he still hoped for more, but God calls him obstinate toward the signs.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.anchor: بسطت له في المال كل البسط، ثم يطمع أن أزيد كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes al-Walīd’s corrupt hope of receiving more.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r1.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { كلا } وهو ردع له عن ذلك الطمع الفاسد

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r2.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r2.claim: Exegetes report that al-Walīd kept declining after this rebuke until he became poor and died poor.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون ولم يزل الوليد في نقصان بعد قوله : { كلا } حتى افتقر ومات فقيرا

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r3.claim: The clause explains the rebuke as a resumption: in answer to “why will he not be increased?”, God says he was hostile to the signs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r3.anchor: إنه تعليل للردع على وجه الاستئناف كأن قائلا قال : لم لا يزاد ؟ فقيل : لأنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r4.claim: ʿAnīd means obstinately opposed, like the related forms al-jalīs, al-akīl, and al-ʿashīr.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r4.anchor: والعنيد في معنى المعاند كالجليس والأكيل والعشير

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r5.claim: The verse indicates that he resisted every proof for divine oneness, justice, power, prophethood, and resurrection, denying them all.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r5.anchor: أنه كان معاندا في جميع الدلائل الدالة على التوحيد والعدل والقدرة وصحة النبوة وصحة البعث

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r6.claim: His was obstinate disbelief: he knew these truths inwardly but denied them with his tongue, which Rāzī calls the worst kind of disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r6.anchor: أن كفره كان كفر عناد كان يعرف هذه الأشياء بقلبه إلا أنه كان ينكرها بلسانه وكفر المعاند أفجش أنواع الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r7.claim: The wording with kāna shows that his hostility had been his established state from long ago.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r7.anchor: ثالثها : أن قوله : { إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا } يدل على أنه من قديم الزمان كان على هذه الحرفة والصنعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r8.claim: The restriction to God’s signs means he specifically opposed divine proofs; Rāzī says this selective hostility, while not opposing other signs, shows his utter loss.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#3/r8.anchor: رابعها : أن قوله : { إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا } يفيد أن تلك المعاندة كانت منه مختصة بآيات الله تعالى وبيناته

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r9.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r9.claim: In al-Walīd’s story, opposing the Prophet means God will cut off the blessings He gave him.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r9.anchor: due to his opposition to the Prophet, God would cut off the blessings He had bestowed upon him

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r10.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r10.claim: “Our signs” can mean the Quran’s verses.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r10.anchor: Our signs means the verses of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r11.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r11.claim: “Our signs” can mean all God’s proofs, including revealed books and prophets.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r11.anchor: all the proofs of God, such as the revealed books and the prophets

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r12.speaker: Āl, IK
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r12.claim: “Our signs” can also refer to God’s blessings.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r12.anchor: or the blessings provided by God

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r1.claim: The man was hostile to God’s signs, meaning the revealed books and messengers, and turned away from the truth.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r1.anchor: الله على خلقه من الكتب والرسل عنيدا، يعني معاندا للحق مجانبا له

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī compares the stubborn opponent to an ʿanūd camel; the cited poem uses al-ʿand for stubbornness.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r2.anchor: كالبعير العنود؛ ومنه قول القائل: إذا نزلت فاجعلاني وسطا … إني كبير لا أطيق العندا

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r3.claim: He derives ʿanīd from ʿānada, meaning to oppose; he compares its form to ʿām qābil, where qābil means coming.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r3.anchor: وهو من عاند معاندة فهو معاند، كما قيل: عام قابل، وإنما هو مقبل

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ʿanīd as one who denies God’s signs.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا} [المدثر: 16] قال: جحودا

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r5.claim: Mujāhid describes him as opposing the signs and standing apart from them.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا} [المدثر: 16] قال محمد بن عمرو: معاندا لها. وقال الحارث: معاندا عنها، مجانبا لها

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r6.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the word as opposing the truth and avoiding it.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله {عنيدا} [المدثر: 16] قال: معاندا للحق مجانبا

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r7.claim: Qatāda calls him ungrateful for and rejecting God’s signs.
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، {إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا} [المدثر: 16] كفورا بآيات الله جحودا بها

TAB-FULL:v23p425/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r8.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p425/r8.claim: Sufyān glosses ʿanīd as one who contends or acts in opposition.

BURSEVI:v10p176/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r5.claim: Kallā rebukes his empty greed, cutting off his failed hope, and connects directly to what precedes.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r5.anchor: ردع وزجر له عن طمعه الفارغ وقطع لرائه الخائب

BURSEVI:v10p176/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r6.claim: ʿAnīd means one who knowingly opposes and rejects truth; here it is equivalent to muʿānd, like other active nouns for one who acts.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r6.anchor: يقال عند خالف الحق ورده عارفا به

BURSEVI:v10p176/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r7.claim: Fronting “Our signs” before ʿanīd restricts the enmity to those signs; this marks extreme loss despite his not opposing everything.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r7.anchor: وتقديم لآياتنا على متعلقه وهو عنيدا يدل على التخصيص

BURSEVI:v10p176/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r8.claim: Defying the clear Quranic signs while denying abundant favors merits total deprivation; his gifts were only gradual entrapment (istidrāj).
BURSEVI:v10p176/r8.anchor: فإن معاندة آيات المنعم وهي الآيات القرآنية مع وضوحها وكفران له مع سبوغها مما يوجب حرمانه بالكلية

BURSEVI:v10p176/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r9.claim: A report says al-Walīd’s wealth kept declining after revelation of this verse until he died poor.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r9.anchor: قيل ما زال بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله حتى هلك وهو فقير

BURSEVI:v10p176/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r10.claim: An unattributed Persian fragment begins by admonishing one who will not heed dear ones’ counsel; the quoted line is incomplete.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r10.anchor: آكس كه نصيحت زعزيزان نكند كوش

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r8.claim: He opposed God's proofs and arguments while recognizing them.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r8.anchor: بحججنا وأدلتنا معاندا ينكرها مع معرفته بها

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda gloss the word as being an obstinate denier.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: عنيدا جحودا عن ابن عباس وقتادة

THALABI:v10p71/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r20.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p71/r20.claim: Al-Walid was stubbornly opposed to God's signs.
THALABI:v10p71/r20.anchor: إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا معنادا سأرهقه صعودا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses kallā as “I will not”; Muqatil says “I will not increase him.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r4.anchor: وهو قوله: {كلا}: قال ابن عباس: لا أفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r5.speaker: المفسرون ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r5.claim: The commentators say al-Walid continued to decline after this refusal; Muqatil says he became poor and died poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r5.anchor: لم يزل الوليد في نقصان بعد قوله: "كلا".

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he stubbornly opposed everything Muhammad brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معاند لكل ما جاء به محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r7.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid kept away from the Quran and did not believe in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان مجانبا للقرآن لا يؤمن به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives ʿanīd from ʿānada, by analogy with jālasa/jalīs and ḍājaʿa/ḍajīʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r8.anchor: وقال المبرد: عاند فهو عنيد، مثل: جالس فهو جليس، وضاجع فهو ضجيع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r6.anchor: { كلا } قطع لرجائه { إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا } للقرآن معاندا غير مطيع.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r7.claim: He stubbornly opposed the Qur’an’s signs and refused obedience.

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r4.claim: Kalla is a particle of rejection, denying a statement, claim, hope, or request; here it cuts off al-Walid's expectation of more.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r4.anchor: Bir sözü, bir davayı veya ümit ve talebi reddeder

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r5.claim: Al-Walid stubbornly opposed either the proofs of the benefactor's oneness or the Quran's verses; this was ingratitude for the blessings.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r5.anchor: o nimetleri veren mün‘imin vahdâniyeti delillerine veya Kur’an âyetlerine karşı inada kalkıştı, bu ise küfrân-ı nimettir

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r6.claim: Ingratitude for blessings leads to their withdrawal, not their increase.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r6.anchor: Nimete küfran ise onun [5455] artmasına değil, kesilmesine sebeptir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.claim: The passage’s general lesson is that gratitude to the giver of blessings is a basic moral duty grounded in reason and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.anchor: Nimete karşı şükretmek, nimet sahibine minnettar olmak en yalın ahlâkî ödevlerden biri, akıl ve adalet gereğidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.claim: Failing to thank God for life and material and spiritual gifts is grave ingratitude, especially when it advances denial, polytheism, and injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.anchor: varlığımızı, hayatımızı, sahip olduğumuz, yararlandığımız her türlü maddî ve mânevî nimet ve imkânları lutfeden Allah’a minnettar olmamak, şükretmemek

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#4/r1.claim: ʿAnīd means stubbornly opposed or defiant.

NAHHAS:v5p65/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p65/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p65/r21.claim: كلا rebukes and restrains his greed for more.

NAHHAS:v5p65/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p65/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p65/r22.claim: عنيدا means stubbornly opposed to God's signs.
NAHHAS:v5p65/r22.anchor: ( إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا ) بمعنى معاند

SAMIN-DURR:74:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:16/r1.claim: This answers why the man does not receive more wealth and why he is rebuked for hoping to gain it: he is hostile to God's signs.
SAMIN-DURR:74:16/r1.anchor: استئناف، جواب لسائل سأل: لم لا يزداد مالا؟ وما باله ردع عن طمعه في ذلك؟

ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r1.claim: The man persistently and knowingly opposes God's messages.

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r1.speaker: Lisan al-'Arab
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r1.claim: Anid denotes someone who opposes or rejects something he knows to be true.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r1.anchor: denotes "one who opposes or rejects something that is true, knowing it to be true" (Lisan al-'Arab)

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r2.claim: Kana implies permanently recurring stubbornness despite its past-tense form; Asad therefore renders verses 18–25 in the present tense.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n7/r2.anchor: the auxiliary verb kana, which indicates here a permanently recurring phenomenon despite its past-tense formulation

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.claim: Meccan opponents repeatedly alleged that the Quran was human fabrication, borrowed ancient lore, or material copied from earlier writings and dictated to Muhammad; the Quran records these charges and reasons against their falsehood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.anchor: ويسجل القرآن مفترياتهم لا يكتمها، ويجادلهم فيها بما يهدي كل ذي عقل وبصيرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r1.claim: The verb عاند is directly transitive, so the lām in لآياتنا is an optional reinforcing lām rather than a required preposition.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r1.anchor: الفعل هو عاند وهو فعل يتعدّى بنفسه (عاندته وعاندت قوله)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r2.claim: A reinforcing lām may mark an object placed before its verb; he illustrates this with 7:154, where the intended object is their Lord.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r2.anchor: الحالة الأولى أن يتقدم المفعول به على فعله كما في قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r3.claim: A reinforcing lām may also follow a deverbal governor, including an active participle or intensive form, as in 35:31 and 11:107.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r3.anchor: والثاني إذا كان العامل فرعاً على الفعل كأن يكون إسم فاعل أو صيغة مبالغة كما في قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r4.claim: The verse meets both conditions: its object precedes the verb and its governor عنيد is an intensive form derived from عاند; the wording does not require بآياتنا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r4.anchor: فيها تقديم وصيغة مبالغة: قدّم المفعول به على الفعل (لآياتنا) والعامل فرع وعلى صيغة مبالغة (عنيد) من عاند

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r5.claim: Grammarians explain the lām as strengthening a weakened syntactic relation when the object is fronted or the governor is derived.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r5.anchor: والغرض منها عند النحاة أن الفعل إذا تقدّم يكون في أقوى حالاته في العمل فإذا تأخر كان أضعف في العمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r6.claim: The author personally prefers the rhetorical explanation that the extra lām intensifies and emphasizes the event itself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p837/r6.anchor: وأنا شخصياً أقول أنها تستعمل لتقوية الحدث فيؤتى باللام الزائدة المؤكِدة زيادة في

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.claim: Al-Muddaththir is the counterpart of the preceding al-Muzzammil; their central themes are essentially the same and their names share a meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes of both sūrahs .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.claim: Verses 11–17 warn that Judgment Day will be severe for disbelievers who presume their wealth and rank will bring them still more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should well inform the people about the afflictions of the Day of Judgement.

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.claim: At the pilgrimage season, Quraysh ask al-Walid for a single story about Muhammad; after rejecting soothsayer, madman, poet, and sorcerer as accurate descriptions, he recommends calling him a sorcerer because people see him as dividing families.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.anchor: ثم إن الوليد بن المغيرة اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش، وكان ذا سن فيهم، وقد حضر الموسم

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the subject as al-Walid and explains that he was a contentious adversary.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في الوليد بن المغيرة وفي ذلك من قوله: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses anīd as stubbornly opposed and contrary; Ru'ba's line about striking the head of al-anad is cited as poetic evidence.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r3.anchor: قال ابن هشام: عنيد: معاند مخالف. قال رؤبة بن العجاج: ونحن ضرابون رأس العند

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r5.claim: Hasan and others say he hoped God would admit him to Paradise, claiming it was created only for him if Muhammad was truthful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وغيره: ثم يطمع أن أدخله الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r7.claim: His greedy desire exposes his vile character and love of worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r7.anchor: وطمعه في الزيادة دليل على مبشعه وحبه للدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r8.claim: His defiance explains the rebuke: he opposed the Benefactor's signs and disbelieved, so a disbeliever does not merit further gifts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r8.anchor: تعليل للردع على وجه الاستئناف، كأن قائلا قال: لم لا يزاد؟ فقال إنه كان يعاند

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r9.claim: The signs could mean God's blessings, matching the gifts listed, but the author prefers Quranic signs because the context concerns his Quranic speech and claim that it is magic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r9.anchor: والأحسن أن يحمل على آيات القرآن لحديثه في القرآن وزعمه أنه سحر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r13.claim: The author points readers to his earlier explanation of عنيد in his commentary on Ibrahim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r13.anchor: وتقدم شرح عنيد في سورة إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r1.claim: “Never” rebukes and restrains him, cutting off his empty expectation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r1.anchor: كلا ردع وزجر له عن طمعه الفارغ وقطع لرجائه الخائب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r2.claim: The declaration that he was obstinate toward God’s signs is an explanatory resumption answering why he was denied further gifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r2.anchor: وقوله سبحانه إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا جملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لتعليل ما قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r3.claim: “Our signs” may mean the proofs of God’s oneness and blessings, or the Qurʾānic verses that al-Walīd disparaged; both show his defiance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r3.anchor: وهي دلائل توحيده أو الآيات القرآنية حيث قال فيها ما قالوا لمعاندة تناسب الإزالة وتمنع من الزيادة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r4.claim: Muqātil says that after this verse was revealed, al-Walīd’s wealth and children kept diminishing until he died.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#5/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل ما زال الوليد بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقص من ماله وولده حتى هلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r3.claim: Kallā rebukes his hope and, as a resumed explanation, grounds the rebuke in defiance of the signs that merited removal of grace and blocked further increase.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r3.anchor: فإنه ردع له عن الطمع وتعليل للردع على سبيل الاستئناف بمعاندة آيات المنعم المناسبة لإزالة النعمة المانعة عن الزيادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r4.claim: It is said that his wealth kept declining after this verse was revealed until he died.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r4.anchor: قيل: ما زال بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان ماله حتى هلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r5.claim: God decisively denies that he will receive more; if he persists, he will instead decline until his death, a prediction that demonstrates the prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r5.anchor: لا تكون له زيادة على ذلك أصلا , وأما النقصان فسيرى إن استمر على تكذيبه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r6.claim: His innate, extreme obstinacy was directed specifically against God’s signs, which guide to divine oneness, rather than against deceptive arguments for shirk.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r6.anchor: لآياتنا } على مالها من العظمة خاصة لكونها هادية إلى الوحدانية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r7.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r7.claim: Al-Malawi defines obstinacy as deviation from the right path and crossing bounds persistently, including opposing truth while knowing it; it may arise from pride, a dry nature, bad character, or impaired reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r7.anchor: والعناد - كما قال الملوي : من كبر في النفس أو يبس في الطبع أو شرائة في الأخلاق

DURR-FULL:v8p327/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r10.claim: Qatada says al-Walid was ungrateful toward God’s signs and denied them.
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses ʿanīd as opposing God’s signs and keeping away from them.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r12.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r12.claim: Abu Malik glosses ʿanīd as one who opposes.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r12.anchor: عن أبي مالك {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira ibn Hisham al-Makhzumi, father of thirteen sons, and says after the hostile verse his person, wealth, and children kept declining until his death.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} الآيات قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة بن هشام المخزومي وكان له ثلاثة عشر ولدا كلهم رب بيت

DURR-FULL:v8p331/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ʿanīd as obstinately denying.
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وهناد بن السري في الزهد وعبد بن حميد عن ابن عباس {عنيدا} قال: جحودا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r7.claim: Mujahid explains that he opposed God's signs and turned away from them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r7.anchor: انه كان لاياتنا عنيدا قال : معاندا عنها مجانبا لها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r10.claim: Saʿīd says that after the verse about his enmity was revealed, al-Walīd continued declining in himself, wealth, and children until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r10.anchor: فلما نزلت انه كان لاياتنا عنيدا لم يزل في ادبار من الدنيا في نفسه وماله وولده حتى أخرجه من الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.claim: The following statement about stubbornness toward God's signs may explain the rebuke: his ingratitude became active opposition, warranting removal of blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.anchor: يجوز أن تكون هذه الجملة تعليلا للردع والإبطال ، أي لأن شدة معاندته لآياتنا كانت كفرانا للنعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.speaker: الماتريدي والمعتزلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.claim: Al-Maturidi and the Muʿtazilites hold that an unbeliever may receive God's favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.anchor: فإن الكافر يكون منعما عليه على المختار وهو قول الماتريدي والمعتزلة خلافا للأشعري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.speaker: الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.claim: Al-Ashʿari differs, denying that an unbeliever receives God's favor in this sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.anchor: وهو قول الماتريدي والمعتزلة خلافا للأشعري ، واختار المحققون أنه خلاف لفظي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.claim: The author follows the careful scholars who regard the disagreement over God's favor to unbelievers as verbal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r16.claim: كلا rebukes and rejects this man's hope for more.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r16.anchor: وقوله تعالى: كلا زجر ورد على أمنية هذا المذكور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r17.claim: He defiantly opposed God's signs and lessons; Ibn Atiyya prefers Quranic verses as the referent because al-Walid later called the Quran magic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r17.anchor: ثم أخبر عنه أنه كان معاندا مخالفا لآيات الله وعبره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r1.claim: Kallā means “I will not”; God withheld wealth and children from him until he died poor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كلا أي لا أفعل فمنعه الله المال والولد حتى مات فقيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r2.anchor: إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا أي معاندا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r3.claim: The signs refer to the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r3.anchor: وفي المراد بالآيات هنا ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه القرآن قاله ابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r4.claim: The signs refer to the truth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r5.claim: The signs refer to the Messenger of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#4/r5.anchor: والثالث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله السدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.claim: Despite all these blessings, he still hoped for more; his hostility means that, knowingly, he disbelieved in response to God’s favors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.anchor: أي: معاندا، وهو الكفر على نعمه بعد العلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r3.claim: ʿAnīd turns away from something out of hostility; it is synonymous with ʿanīd and muʿānd.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r3.anchor: والعنيد: الذاهب عن الشيء على طريق العداوة له، عند يعند عنودا، وهو عاند

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.claim: Abundant blessings make disobedience toward the Benefactor more serious.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على أن كثرة النعم توجب عظم عصيان المنعم.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.claim: An increase in blessings can become a source of corruption.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن مزيد النعم قد يكون مفسدة لذلك قال: (ثم يطمع أن أزيد (15) كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا (16).

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability is shown by enemies’ failure to meet the challenge despite intense opposition; they resort to insults and fighting instead of rebuttal.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.anchor: وتدل على إعجاز القرآن؛ لأنهم مع شدة عداوتهم لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -،

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.claim: Calling unbelief an attempt to invalidate truth bad supports Abu Hashim’s view that reflection can be bad, against Abu Ali.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن الكفر لإبطال الحق يقبح، فتدل على قول أبي هاشم: إن في النظر ما يقبح، خلاف قول أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.claim: Thinking and grimacing are acts performed by the human servant.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.anchor: وتدل أن الفكر والعبوس فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r22.claim: كلا rebukes him and cuts off expectation of further gifts.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r23.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r23.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r23.claim: His hostility to God's signs explains the rebuke: an ungrateful disbeliever does not deserve an increase.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r24.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r24.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r24.claim: A report says his wealth kept diminishing after this verse until his death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r24.anchor: ما زال بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله حتى هلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r29.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r29.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies God's signs as the Quran.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r30.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r30.claim: Al-Suddi identifies God's signs as Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r30.anchor: الثاني : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r31.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r31.claim: Mujahid identifies God's signs as the truth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r32.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r32.claim: Mujahid and Abu Ubayda gloss anid as obstinate; the passage cites al-Harith as poetic evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r32.anchor: أحدها : معاند , قاله مجاهد وأبو عبيدة , وأنشد قول الحارثي :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r1.claim: The quoted line completes the preceding citation offered for the sense of anid as obstinate.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r1.anchor: صبحنا تميما غداة الجفار … بشهباء ملمومة باسرة

MUQATIL:74:11-17/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r6.claim: He was hostile to the Qur'an's signs, turning away from them and refusing to believe in the Qur'an.
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r6.anchor: يعني كان عن آيات القرآن معرضا مجانبا له لا يؤمن بالقرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r1.claim: “كلا” cuts off his hope: after this he will not receive more blessings while persisting in disbelief; his wealth and status declined until he died.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r1.anchor: ردع له وقطع لرجائه أي لا يجمع له بعد اليوم بين الكفر والمزيد من النعم فلم يزل بعد نزول الآية في نقصان من المال والجاه حتى هلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r2.claim: His obstinate denial of God's signs explains the rebuke: an ingrate who rejects the Benefactor's signs does not deserve further increase.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#5/r2.anchor: وهو تعليل الردع على وجه الاستئناف كان قائلا قال لما لا يزال فقيل إنه جحد آيات المنعم وكفر بذلك نعمته والمكافر لا يستحق المزيد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r6.claim: The direct sense is God will not increase his gifts because al-Walid disbelieves in His favors.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r6.anchor: أي ليس يكون ذلك مع كفره بالنعم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r8.claim: Qurtubi says al-Walid’s wealth and children kept diminishing until he died.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r8.anchor: فلم يزل يرى النقصان في ماله وولده حتى هلك

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r12.claim: Kalla may close hope of increase and connect to preceding words, or mean “indeed” and begin the next statement.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r12.anchor: وقيل: { كلا } بمعنى حقا ويكون ابتداء

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r13.claim: Al-Walid is obstinate toward Muhammad and revelation; Mujahid glosses ʿanid as rejecting known truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r13.anchor: يقال: عاند فهو عنيد مثل جالس فهو جليس قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r14.claim: ʿAnid opposes or rejects known truth; the root describes a camel straying from its path.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r14.anchor: وعند يعند بالكسر أي خالف ورد الحق وهو يعرفه فهو عنيد وعاند

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r2.claim: ʿAnīd means intensely obstinate and opposed to what is right, from a verb for disputing clear truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r2.anchor: الشديد العناد وهو المخالفة للصواب وهو فعيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.claim: His obstinacy was his effort to discredit the Qur’an as magic, poetry, or soothsaying despite knowing it was none of these.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r3.anchor: هو محاولته الطعن في القرآن وتحيله للتمويه بأنه سحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r5.claim: His thinking and devising explains and completes the statement that he was obstinate toward God’s signs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.claim: The worldly threat follows his worldly motives of leadership and envy; the threat of Hell follows his attacks on the Qur’an and denial of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.anchor: وقد وزع وعيده على ما تقتضيه أعماله فإنه لما ذكر عناده وهو من مقاصده السيئة
